title: Tiered prefetch priority lattice — scratch draft
body:
Purpose / context:
This is a messy personal sketch for a client-side + proxy prefetch strategy that treats session context items as a small lattice of priorities. Goal is to reduce median tail latency for interactive LLM apps while keeping token / network costs bounded and making behavior predictable under constrained connectivity. This is NOT final; lots of rough heuristics and trade-offs enumerated for later cleaning into a proper API and config schema.

Top-level goals:
- Fast cold-start for common user flows (chat startup, code assist init).
- Graceful degradation under bandwidth limits: prefer context items that give most model utility per byte.
- Deterministic ordering so rollouts / A/B tests are reproducible.
- Configurable by product/team: different apps want different trade-offs.

High-level idea (one-line):
Represent candidate context fragments (user messages, embeddings, KB snippets, tool state blobs) as nodes in a 3D priority lattice (importance, recency, cost). Compute a scalar rank via configurable projection and prefetch until budget exhausted.

Primitive types (what we might prefetch / warm):
- recent_user_turn: raw most-recent messages (cheap, high importance)
- condensed_memory: compressed user profile / preferences (medium cost, high long-term value)
- embeddings_chunk: precomputed vector block for a document range (cost = bytes + compute if on-device recompute)
- tool_state: small JSON for connected tools (e.g., calendar snapshot)
- model_cache_key: cached KV prefix for model on the edge (large but can speed token generation)

Priority lattice axes (each 0..1 normalized):
- importance_score: product of signal sources (explicit user focus, feature flags, intent detector)
- recency_score: inverse time-decay; short half-life for conversational turns, slower for profile info
- cost_score: inverse of estimated bytes + decode cost (higher if cheap, lower if expensive)

Scoring projection (configurable):
We want a scalar rank r = w1*importance + w2*recency + w3*(1 - cost)  (weights sum to 1)
Where weights are per-route or per-product. Default: w1=0.5, w2=0.3, w3=0.2.

Budgeting model:
- Two budgets: network_budget_bytes (per-session ephemeral) and background_cpu_budget_ms.
- Policy: select top-ranked candidates until network_budget depleted.
- Soft-degradation: reserve 10% budget for immediate-turn items to avoid starving live messages.

API / config sketch (textified JSON example):
client.prefetch.configure({
  "route": "editor-autocomplete",
  "weights": {"importance":0.55, "recency":0.25, "cost":0.20},
  "network_budget": 64_000,           // bytes per session warm-up
  "cpu_budget_ms": 50,               // local CPU budget for compression/embeddings
  "min_reserve_for_immediate": 0.1,  // fraction reserve
  "ttl_seconds": 1800,               // freshness window for prefetched items
  "consistency": "best_effort"      // options: strict / best_effort / eventual
});

Client selection flow (sketch):
1) Discover candidate fragments from local state, server-provided hints (route hints), and background index.
2) For each candidate compute normalized axes: importance, recency, estimated_cost.
3) Compute r and sort descending.
4) Prefetch in order until network_budget - reserved_capacity <= 0.
5) Mark prefetched items with metadata: origin, score, fetched_at, ttl.

Prefetch metadata (text field layout):
- id: uuid
- type: one of primitive types
- origin_hint: "kb/selector", "last-turn-extractor", "server-hint"
- score: float
- size_bytes: int
- expires_at: iso8601
- integrity_hash: base64

Edge/proxy behavior notes:
- Proxy should accept clients' candidate lists plus optional priority override token (signed) from backend systems when available.
- Proxy can do opportunistic batching across users on same tenant (careful: privacy isolation). Prefer dedup by hash when two clients request same chunk.
- Telemetry: per-prefetch success/failure, bytes saved on generation (if measurable), and time between fetch and use (to evaluate utility).

Heuristics and special cases:
- Adaptive cost model: when network is CPU-constrained (e.g., low-end devices), increase cost_score penalty for CPU-heavy precomputes (embeddings).
- Cold-device detection: if device has not been online for > 24h, favor small profile blobs over large doc embeddings.
- Interactive-high-priority: when client is in interactive mode (typing), reduce background prefetch intensity and reserve bandwidth for immediate-turn retrieval.
- Cohort-level tuning: experiments may adjust weight vector per cohort; store weights in remote config and validate via shadow runs.

ASCII diagram (very rough):

  Importance ->    * high importance candidates    * low importance
                   |                             |
  Recency ^        +-----------------------------+   time decays left->right
     |             |  [A] recents  [B] cond mem  |
     |             |  [C] embeddings [D] tool   |
     v             +-----------------------------+
  Cost low ->  cheaper items on top-left (fast wins), expensive bottom-right (skip unless high importance)

Open questions / risks:
- How to quantify "utility" per byte? We need offline eval datasets where we can measure perplexity delta or task success delta given different context subsets.
- Privacy boundary: server-supplied hints may leak; need signed tokens or ACL checks.
- Staleness vs cost: embeddings may be stale quickly for mutable docs; TTLs must be conservative or we need freshness checks.
- Multi-device coherence: if device A prefetched and edited a doc, device B may have stale prefetch; we need versioned ids.

Next steps / TODOs for a proper PRD:
- Collect telemetry prototype: implement lightweight prefetch scoring in the experimental client lib and surface metrics for bytes fetched vs bytes used and usefulness.
- Design server hint API: compact candidate bundle with signed priority overrides and per-item freshness tags.
- Draft a minimal wire-level prefetch manifest schema (protobuf) and map to current session sync payloads.
- Run a small A/B on editor-autocomplete: baseline vs lattice prefetch (target cohorts: 5k users).

Notes to self (quick):
- keep default weights biased to importance; recency useful for chat but less for profile data.
- avoid embedding precompute on-device unless explicit opt-in.
- consider having a "micro-prefetch" class: <1KB items that are always allowed regardless of budget.

References / inspirations:
- Some papers on bandwidth-aware caching for edge ML (TODO: add links later)
- internal: GH:repo/session-proxy#204 has prior prototype bits

End of scratchpad — will refine into a clean API sketch once experiments give us telemetry.
